tagline: Strategic investment holding company managing diversified portfolio including core stakes in Volkswagen and Porsche AG, with expanding technology and defense investments
hero_kpi_rationale: Porsche SE manages two key performance indicators: adjusted group net result after taxes and consolidated net debt, direct reflections of its sustainable value creation strategy for shareholders.

kpis.name: Adjusted group net result after taxes
kpis.explanation: Core earnings metric reflecting profitability of the Porsche SE Group, adjusted for special factors. Key management KPI as stated in the 2025 annual report.
kpis.description: Porsche SE's adjusted group net result for fiscal year 2025 amounted to 2.894 billion euros, down 8.2% compared to the prior year (2024: 3.151 billion EUR). This decline reflects macroeconomic headwinds, protectionist measures (notably US tariffs), and intensified competitive pressures affecting core portfolio holdings. The result remains a key management indicator for the diversified investment platform.
kpis.signal: Solid core profitability despite challenging macroeconomic environment and geopolitical headwinds

kpis.name: Consolidated group net debt
kpis.explanation: Consolidated net debt position of the Porsche SE Group as of December 31, including financial liabilities net of cash and cash equivalents. Key balance sheet metric.
kpis.description: Porsche SE Group's consolidated net debt amounted to 5.099 billion euros as of December 31, 2025, slightly declining 1.2% compared to December 31, 2024 (5.160 billion EUR). This improvement reflects successful refinancing measures from the prior year and demonstrates solid financing of the investment platform. Management forecasts net debt between 4.7 and 5.2 billion EUR as of December 31, 2026.
kpis.signal: Strong financial foundation with stable net debt position and successful refinancing measures

kpis.name: Net asset value
kpis.explanation: NAV represents the aggregate value of Porsche SE's portfolio holdings and other assets less liabilities, reflecting the underlying value of the investment platform.
kpis.description: Porsche SE's net asset value amounted to 17.846 billion euros as of December 31, 2025, up 4.9% compared to 2024 (17.019 billion EUR). This increase notably reflects growing valuation of portfolio holdings, with book value nearly doubling to approximately 535 million euros since end-2024. Strategic expansion in defense and technology sectors contributes to strengthening long-term value creation potential.
kpis.signal: Growing underlying value of diversified investment portfolio with portfolio holdings book value nearly doubled

kpis.name: Holding premium
kpis.explanation: The holding discount represents the difference between NAV and market capitalization as a percentage of NAV, indicating the market's valuation of the holding company structure.
kpis.description: The holding premium stands at 31% as of December 31, 2025, representing significant improvement of 11.4 percentage points compared to 2024 (35%). This discount reduction reflects improved market perception regarding the holding structure and value creation potential of Porsche SE's diversified investment platform, notably driven by portfolio holdings achieving unicorn status (valuations of at least 1 billion euros).
kpis.signal: Narrowing discount reflects improving investor perception of holding company structure and portfolio value creation

kpis.name: Debt-to-asset ratio
kpis.explanation: LTV ratio measures net debt as a percentage of NAV, reflecting the financial leverage of the investment platform and debt capacity.
kpis.description: The LTV ratio (net debt relative to net asset value) stands at 22.2% as of December 31, 2025, improving 4.7 percentage points compared to 2024 (23.3%). This ratio reflects a comfortable leverage position and demonstrates Porsche SE's financial flexibility to pursue its diversified investment strategy, particularly in strategic sectors such as European defense and cutting-edge technologies.
kpis.signal: Comfortable leverage position with improving debt-to-asset ratio, supporting financial flexibility for strategic expansion

kpis.name: Dividends received
kpis.explanation: Dividend income received from portfolio investments, primarily from core stakes in Volkswagen AG and Porsche AG, reflecting cash returns on strategic holdings.
kpis.description: Dividends received by Porsche SE during fiscal year 2025 amounted to 1.006 billion euros, down 40.9% compared to 2024 (1.703 billion EUR). This decline reflects reduced distributions from core holdings, notably Volkswagen AG and Porsche AG, due to operational challenges and difficult macroeconomic environment characterized by geopolitical uncertainties and protectionist measures.
kpis.signal: Dividend income decline reflects reduced distributions from core holdings amid challenging operating environment

kpis.name: Dividends paid
kpis.explanation: Total dividend distributions paid to shareholders during the fiscal year, reflecting shareholder remuneration policy.
kpis.description: Dividends paid to Porsche SE shareholders during fiscal year 2025 amounted to 584 million euros, down 25.4% compared to 2024 (783 billion EUR). Despite a challenging operating environment, management maintains its commitment to shareholders by proposing a distribution for fiscal year 2025 of 1.510 EUR per preference share and 1.504 EUR per ordinary share.
kpis.signal: Dividend payout maintained despite earnings pressures, demonstrating commitment to shareholder returns

kpis.name: Dividend per preference share
kpis.explanation: Annual dividend distribution per preference share for fiscal year 2025, proposed to shareholders for approval at Annual General Meeting.
kpis.description: The proposed dividend per preference share for fiscal year 2025 amounts to 1.510 EUR, down 20.9% compared to 2024 (1.910 EUR). This reduction reflects management's cautious approach facing macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties, while maintaining attractive shareholder remuneration. For fiscal year 2026, management forecasts adjusted results between 1.5 and 3.5 billion euros.
kpis.signal: Dividend reduction reflects cautious capital allocation amid uncertain macroeconomic outlook for 2026

kpis.name: Group net result after taxes
kpis.explanation: IFRS consolidated net profit of Porsche SE Group including special items and one-time effects from portfolio revaluations.
kpis.description: Porsche SE Group's net result after taxes amounted to 2.651 billion euros for fiscal year 2025, representing exceptional improvement compared to fiscal year 2024 which showed a loss of 20.017 billion euros. This substantial improvement notably reflects positive revaluation of portfolio holdings, with book value nearly doubling, as well as absence of impairment charges that impacted the prior year. IFRS result includes special effects and one-time items related to portfolio revaluations.
kpis.signal: Significant recovery from prior year loss, reflecting improved valuation of portfolio holdings

kpis.name: Headcount - Porsche SE (holding)
kpis.explanation: Number of employees directly employed by Porsche SE as a holding company, excluding consolidated subsidiaries and investments.
kpis.description: Porsche SE maintains a lean holding structure with 38 employees, reflecting its role as strategic portfolio manager. Operational activities are delegated to consolidated subsidiaries including Porsche Beteiligung GmbH and its subsidiaries. This minimalist holding structure enables efficient management of strategic investments in Volkswagen AG, Porsche AG, and the diversified investment portfolio.
kpis.signal: Lean holding structure with operational management delegated to subsidiaries

kpis.name: Dividend per share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share, aggregated from yfinance.dividends across the seven most recent fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 1.91 EUR in prior year.

kpis.name: Capital returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, sourced from yfinance.cashflow across the four most recent fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 0.584 billion EUR in prior year.

kpis.name: Payout ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio: Dividends paid / Net result, calculated across the three most recent fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net result distributed as dividends: 22.0% in prior year.

risks.title: Conflicts of interest within supervisory board
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly mentioned mid-report with direct language (potential conflicts of interest); stable trend, this type of conflict from dual mandates is structural; governance/key person category carries moderate weight but risk is concrete and documented by actual 2025 case.

risks.title: Impairment of VW and Porsche AG holdings
risks.score_rationale: Risk positioned late in report but highlighted as major audit discussion topic with strong language (significant discussion point); trend increasing as non-monetary impairments were actually recognized in 2025; capital/valuation category carries strong weight for a pure holding company.

risks.title: Risk of non-detection of existence-threatening risks
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned mid-report within audit committee framework with vigilance language (early detection of existence-threatening risks); stable trend, recurring control; operational/industrial risk category carries moderate weight but company's survival explicitly referenced.

risks.title: Tax risk from corporate income tax rate changes
risks.score_rationale: Identified as priority audit point mid-report with precise language (deferred tax assessment considering corporate income tax rate change); trend new due to rate change; regulatory/tax category carries strong weight.

risks.title: Portfolio concentration in two holdings
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk present throughout report with factual but revealing language (impairment tests of Volkswagen AG and Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG holdings); stable trend but aggravated by 2025 impairments; capital category carries strong weight for holding whose value depends almost exclusively on two assets.

ai_positioning.summary: Porsche SE supports strategic integration of AI and defense technologies through its holdings in Volkswagen and Porsche AG, as well as through expansion in European technology startup financing. Emphasis is on incremental innovation and strategic diversification rather than direct disruption.
evidence: Growing investments in European technology startups via DTCP Defense Fund (100 million EUR in 2026)
Focus on software solutions, cybersecurity, and autonomous systems in defense sector
Indirect AI support via autonomous vehicles and digital services at Porsche AG and Volkswagen
Six portfolio holdings achieving unicorn status (valuations exceeding 1 billion EUR)
